statement: The function returns a result r and r = max { A(v) | 0 <= v < n }, where A(v) is defined as follows: if v = headID then A(v) = 0; otherwise form the unique list v, manager[v], manager[manager[v]], ..., headID obtained by repeatedly applying manager until headID is reached, and let A(v) be the sum of informTime[u] over all entries u of this list except the first entry v (i.e., the sum over all proper ancestors of v). Equivalently, A(v) is the minute at which employee v learns the news, and r is the maximum such minute.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 100000; headID is an integer with 0 <= headID < n; len(manager) = n and len(informTime) = n; manager[headID] = -1; for every i with 0 <= i < n and i != headID, 0 <= manager[i] < n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= informTime[i] <= 1000; the directed graph with an edge manager[i] -> i for each i != headID is a tree rooted at headID (equivalently, starting from any employee and repeatedly taking manager reaches headID and no cycle occurs); and informTime[i] = 0 for every employee i with no direct subordinate (i.e., with no j such that 0 <= j < n and manager[j] = i).

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail (no panic, arithmetic overflow, or out-of-bounds access occurs).
